data.narrative:
Eridu is a Series A-stage semiconductor company founded by Drew Perkins and Omar Hassen that has raised approximately $230M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 3 public semiconductor players (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private-stage peers, with particular focus on same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies including Rebellions ($2.3B Series A), d-Matrix ($2.0B Series A), and Positron AI ($1.0B Series B).

Two valuation methods were applicable. Stage-progression methodology, using total capital raised as a proxy baseline and applying a typical 2.0x Series A step-up multiplier, implies a valuation of $460M. Peer-median benchmarking across the 3 identified same-sector comparables yielded a median valuation of $2.0B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.3B. Public-comparable anchoring via price-to-sales multiples (18.9x median across the sector) could not be applied due to absence of disclosed revenue figures, standard for private companies at this stage.

Triangulation across applicable methods supports a valuation range of $391M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median point of $1.2B. The substantial spread reflects meaningful uncertainty around whether Eridu's competitive positioning and market traction more closely align with earlier-stage private comps or the upper tier represented by Rebellions. Key unknowns include revenue run-rate, customer concentration, and technical differentiation relative to named peers.
